blocks.text: B1-22 · Formal letters and emails
Lesson overview

In A2-22 You wrote the first brief formal emails. Now write complete letters: with place and date, recipient, object, opening formula, a body organized in paragraphs, closure and attachments. Learn the formulas for the most common types of letter (information request, registration, complaint, apology, thanksgiving, candidacy), the forms of courtesy of the standard Arabic ( ⁧أَرْجُو التَّكَرُّمَ بِـ⁩ …, ⁧يُسْعِدُنِي أَنْ⁩ …, ⁧وَتَفَضَّلُوا بِقَبُولِ⁩ ...) and the difference between formal letter, semi-formal email and informal message. On examination B1 The formal letter is one of the two writing tests. Two weeks.

rows: B1 · Module B1.4 "Write, speak, open sources"
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 143–144), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G57, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. set up a complete Arab formal letter, with all its parts;
2. choose opening and closing formulas suitable for the recipient;
3. write letters of request, complaint, apology, thanks and candidacy;
4. from an informal register to a formal register ( ⁧أُرِيدُ⁩ → ⁧أَوَدُّ أَنْ⁩ …; ⁧أَرْسِلُوا⁩ → ⁧أَرْجُو التَّكَرُّمَ بِإِرْسَالِ⁩ …);
5. write a formal letter of 120–150 words, clear, courteous and without dialect.
Two-week plan.

2. The structure of the formal letter

rows: Thanking you for your cooperation, waiting for your answer

blocks.text: Order. In an Arabic letter the object ( ⁧المَوْضُوع⁩ ) comes before the greeting; the consignee goes on a separate line, to the right; the closing and signature at the bottom left (in writing from right to left, i.e. at the end of the line). In an email, the ... object field replaces the line ⁧المَوْضُوع⁩ .

an unknown recipient ⁧إِلَى مَنْ يَهُمُّهُ الأَمْرُ⁩

8. The email
closure ⁧سَلَامٌمَعَ أَطْيَبِ التَّحِيَّاتِوَتَفَضَّلُوا بِقَبُولِ فَائِقِ الاِحْتِرَامِ⁩ ⁧إِلَى اللِّقَاءِ⁩ ·

The email object is short and nominal (B1-15): ⁧طَلَبُ شَهَادَةِ حُضُورٍ⁩ · ⁧اِسْتِفْسَارٌ عَنِ السَّكَنِ⁩ · ⁧تَعْدِيلُ مَوْعِدِ المُقَابَلَةِ⁩ . Avoid in a formal email: dialect words, abbreviations, emojis, phrases without greeting.
9. The Register
1. The plural of respect. To a formal recipient we address the plural: ⁧إِلَيْكُمْ⁩ , ⁧رَدُّكُمْ⁩ , ⁧تَفَضَّلُوا⁩ , even if it is a
lonely. You write to the singular ( ⁧أَنَا⁩ ), unless he writes on behalf of an office ( ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ ).
2. The verbs of courtesy. ⁧تَكَرَّمَ⁩ • have courtesy • • ⁧تَفَضَّلَ⁩ "Dignified' means: ⁧يُسْعِدُنِي⁩ , ⁧يُشَرِّفُنِي⁩ I have the honor.
3. The nominal style. The maṣdar make the text more formal and shorter: ⁧أَرْجُو إِرْسَالَ⁩ ... instead of ⁧أَرْجُو أَنْ تُرْسِلُوا⁩ ….
4. No dialect. The words you use every day in Egyptian (ʿāyiz, mumkin, ḫalāṣ) do not enter a letter
formal.
10. Pronunciation

Read a letter aloud (for example, dictate it to someone or read it over the phone): formulas are read with desinences, because they are fixed: taḥiyyatan ṭayyibatan wa-baʿdu · wa-tafaḍḍalū bi-qabūli fāʾiqi l-iḥtirām. Exercise to breathe, with a break only before ⁧وَبَعْدُ⁩ .

f. · pl. ⁧مَصَالِح⁩ · ⁧لِمَصْلَحَةِ⁩ In the case of a vessel, the following points are added:

Notes of use. ⁧عُذْرًا⁩ It is the short and courteous excuse, even by voice (sorry), ⁧اِعْتِذَار⁩ It's the formal written excuse. ⁧مَصْلَحَة⁩ in Egypt also indicates a public office: ⁧مَصْلَحَةُ الجَوَازَاتِ⁩ The passport office is located in the centre of the city. ⁧ظُرُوف⁩ often appears with ⁧طَارِئ⁩ Unexpected: ⁧لِظُرُوفٍ طَارِئَةٍ⁩ For unforeseen circumstances, this is the case.
